title: Paal Kesari (milk sweet)
lead: Paal kesari is something I came across only recently. It's a really creative play on kesari that takes it to the next level, rich enough to be offered as prasadam.
story: Growing up, my mom made kesari for every occasion: a birthday, a celebration, the end of school exams. Kesari has such a fond, comforting spot in my heart, and it comes together so fast. This is the simplest sweet in the whole lot: just milk, sugar, rava and ghee, all in one pan. No roasting, no nuts, nothing fancy. (adapted from Rakesh Raghunathan's milk sweet recipe)
ingredientsTitle: What you need (use the same cup for everything; the magic number is 4-3-1-1)
steps: In a pan, mix the milk, sugar and rava with half the ghee. Don't roast the rava. That's what keeps this sweet a beautiful milky white.
Stir until the sugar dissolves, then put the pan on the stove.
Cook on a low flame and keep stirring without stopping. It's a real workout for the hands! It comes to a boil, then slowly thickens as the rava swells up.
Add the rest of the ghee a little at a time, mixing well each time, until it thickens and leaves the sides of the pan.
Transfer to another dish and let it cool. Serve it hot or at room temperature.
tip: 4 milk, 3 sugar, 1 rava, 1 ghee. Skip the dry fruits, saffron and cardamom. The milk and ghee are the whole flavor here.
closing: That's it. The paal kesari is ready.

nutrition.yield: Makes about 1.3 kg, or roughly 26 pieces of 50 g (about 207 kcal each).
